headline: High-risk workspace sharing: Cline can write and browse broadly while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable docs artifact, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure if its content is fed into Cline.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a docs-only knowledge list with no runtime defenses or isolation; B can read/write workspace files, run browsers, and use MCP. If A’s content is copied into B’s workspace or MCP inputs, B may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pair has no documented shared channel, so this is possible but not default.
conditions: IF A’s content is placed into B’s workspace files or MCP payloads, THEN B can parse it as instructions.
IF the operator manually bridges A into B via copy-paste or file import, THEN injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Keep A content out of B’s active workspace.
Use a read-only export for A summaries.
Strip instructions from imported text before B reads it.
Disable MCP sources that ingest untrusted text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between A and B.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B reads workspace files, uses browsers, and can send context to configured model providers/MCP servers. If sensitive workspace content is shared with B, it can leave the local environment through those channels. A is not a leak source, but its docs can still be copied into B’s broader data flow.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in B’s workspace, THEN B can read them and transmit derived context to external services.
IF B is connected to a third-party model provider or MCP server, THEN workspace content may leave the host.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace.
Use a separate workspace for sensitive files.
Disable external model providers for sensitive tasks.
Audit MCP servers before enabling them.
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory data egress controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable, so it cannot write; B has unrestricted filesystem write, modify_git_state, and shared-state-by-filesystem concurrency. There is no locking or coordination primitive in A, and B’s defaults allow concurrent workspace mutation. The main conflict is among B instances, but the pair still inherits the same shared filesystem write surface and git-state risk.
conditions: IF two B instances operate on the same workspace, THEN file and git conflicts can occur.
IF A-derived files are introduced into the workspace, THEN B may overwrite or reorder them without coordination.
mitigations: Use one B instance per workspace.
Commit or stash before parallel edits.
Lock the workspace during automated runs.
Keep A-derived artifacts read-only.
requires-engineering: add file-level locking and git coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can supply curated links or text, and B can browse, write files, and act on tool outputs. If B treats A’s content as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits or browser actions. A itself cannot execute, so the harm depends on B’s downstream authority, but B’s default tool loop makes this pathway plausible.
conditions: IF B uses A’s output as a source of truth without verification, THEN incorrect facts can propagate into edits or browser actions.
IF A’s links are stale or misleading, THEN B may act on them and produce incorrect work products.
mitigations: Require B to verify A-sourced claims before acting.
Mark A output as untrusted reference material.
Cross-check links in a browser before editing.
Limit B to read-only review for A-derived tasks.
requires-engineering: add citation verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for A, and B’s profile only shows general workspace/browser data handling. The pair therefore has no evidenced compliance breach pathway beyond ordinary operational handling. Because A is docs-only and B’s compliance posture is unspecified, this remains a low-confidence, low-severity gap rather than a documented violation.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into B’s workspace, THEN compliance review is required.
IF B is configured to retain browser screenshots or model logs, THEN retention policy must be checked.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workspace.
Review B’s logging settings.
Disable screenshot capture for sensitive tasks.
Confirm model-provider terms before use.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
